paths.description: Homepage discovery archetype and consent-first load; covers first impression, navigation, metadata, performance, privacy, and preferences.
Homepage narrow form-factor condition; covers viewport/reflow/touch usability.
Browse directory listing archetype; represents category/listing and search discovery.
Live channel/player archetype; represents the primary anonymous watch journey.
Nonexistent channel route; covers unavailable-content messaging and recovery.

Login entry interaction was attempted only to inspect the public modal boundary; authenticated account, purchase, subscription, and cancellation flows were not covered because no credentials or payment context were provided.

findings.summary: The interface stays in its dark theme when the user requests a light color scheme.
findings.evidence: The light-preference screenshot remains dark, and computed CSS reports body color-scheme: dark with no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose an automatic system theme using color-scheme and prefers-color-scheme, while retaining an explicit user override.

findings.summary: Continuous animations remain active under reduced-motion.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe found thirteen running animations, mostly 2 seconds long, and no prefers-reduced-motion rule in accessible stylesheets.
findings.suggestedFix: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, stop auto-advance and non-essential looping motion and shorten necessary state transitions.

findings.summary: Route and major state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no view-transition rules or names across the rendered homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance directory/channel route and modal state changes with the View Transitions API, preserving an instant fallback.

findings.summary: Navigation chrome does not expose scroll-aware feedback.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no scroll-state container query, progress cue, or declarative scroll-position response on a long discovery feed.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state queries or a lightweight progress/affordance treatment where the long feed makes position ambiguous.

findings.summary: Consent and transient surfaces are implemented without native dialog/popover primitives.
findings.evidence: The live DOM reported 0 dialog elements and 0 popover elements while the page displayed a large consent surface and custom transient controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for modal flows and popover with declarative light-dismiss for transient menus, preserving focus and Escape behavior.

findings.summary: The desktop page omits the viewport meta tag and is scaled down on a 360px screen.
findings.evidence: At a requested 360x800 viewport, layout reported hasViewportMeta:false and a 980 CSS-pixel layout viewport; the screenshot shows tiny desktop text and controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width=device-width, initial-scale=1 and deliver a genuinely narrow responsive layout rather than browser shrink-to-fit.

findings.summary: Reusable discovery components show no container-query adaptation.
findings.evidence: Accessible stylesheet inspection found no @container rules while the same cards/sidebar patterns appear across homepage and directory layouts.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce size containers around reusable card and rail regions and adapt them with @container rules where their available width differs.

findings.summary: Many controls become undersized for touch and several controls have very small hit boxes.
findings.evidence: The interaction probe found many controls below 24px high, including 17px links and 20px tags; shrink-to-fit mobile rendering makes them smaller still.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 24x24 CSS-pixel targets, preferably 44x44 for primary touch controls, and retain visible focus styles.

findings.summary: Cold-load performance is poor under Lighthouse mobile conditions.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 9.2s, FCP 6.4s, TBT 540ms, and time-to-interactive 12.3s, producing a 0.44 performance score.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP and interaction path, prioritize the LCP resource, and defer non-critical work until after the primary content is usable.

findings.summary: Large layout shifts occur during representative page loads.
findings.evidence: The layout primitive measured CLS 0.373 on the homepage mobile condition and 1.122 on the directory, with multiple shifts after 1.3s.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve space for late content, include intrinsic image dimensions/aspect ratios, and use stable font fallbacks.

findings.summary: Heavy scripting blocks the main thread.
findings.evidence: The trace recorded 8 long tasks, a 179ms longest task, and 399.76ms total blocking time; Lighthouse independently measured 540ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Break large tasks into prioritized chunks and defer discovery, ads, casting, and below-fold work until needed.

findings.summary: The initial route ships an expensive script-heavy dependency graph.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 252 requests and 2.92MB transferred, including 148 scripts totaling 2.02MB; numerous parser-inserted classic scripts were confirmed in the body without async/defer.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the initial route graph, load non-critical chunks conditionally, and apply intentional script priority/defer semantics.

findings.summary: JavaScript dominates the initial transfer and includes legacy/polyfill bundles.
findings.evidence: HAR shows 148 scripts and 2.02MB of script transfer; DOM inspection confirms both nomodulePolyfills and a separate polyfills bundle on the page.
findings.suggestedFix: Use coverage and bundle analysis to remove unused/duplicate code and avoid shipping legacy polyfills to capable browsers.

findings.summary: Mobile reflow and target sizing are not usable at the requested narrow viewport.
findings.evidence: The 360px capture is a 980px desktop canvas scaled to 0.367, making text and interactive targets materially too small even though no horizontal scrollbar is exposed.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore device-width reflow and audit text, player controls, captions, and targets at 320-400 CSS pixels and 200% zoom.

findings.summary: Images omit intrinsic dimensions and responsive delivery metadata.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found all 31 images missing both width and height, 15 missing srcset, 13 oversized, and 5 missing alt attributes; Lighthouse also flagged low-resolution images.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio, add responsive sources, and review each missing alt as decorative or meaningful.

findings.summary: Browser hygiene issues include BFCache prevention and missing source maps.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed valid-source-maps, inspector-issues, and BFCache, reporting one back/forward cache failure reason.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove avoidable BFCache blockers, publish valid production source maps to the error tooling boundary, and clear DevTools Issues.

findings.summary: Public content is effectively absent from raw HTML and the mobile viewport signal is missing.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured only 1% rendered-word coverage, isJsShell:true, and a crawler screenshot with no meaningful stream/category content; the viewport meta is also absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render or statically emit meaningful channel/category links and text, and add a correct viewport meta tag.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie attributes leave material gaps.
findings.evidence: Headers show no CSP, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. Cookie evidence includes a non-Secure country cookie and an api_token cookie without HttpOnly; all six use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, explicit Referrer/Permissions policies, and minimize cookie scope; make sensitive cookies Secure, HttpOnly, and Lax/Strict unless cross-site use is essential.

findings.summary: The pre-choice load has a broad data and third-party request surface.
findings.evidence: Network capture recorded 249 cross-origin requests and 2.85MB cross-origin transfer, including ad and telemetry endpoints; the consent panel names up to 109 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Block non-essential advertising/analytics until consent, minimize partner access, batch telemetry, and document purpose/retention by endpoint.

findings.summary: Defensive browser policy coverage is incomplete.
findings.evidence: HSTS, nosniff, and SAMEORIGIN are present, but CSP/frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy are absent from the main response.
findings.suggestedFix: Add CSP with frame-ancestors, an explicit strict referrer policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy; evaluate Trusted Types for this large SPA.

findings.summary: Core public content disappears without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Raw HTML contains 1% of rendered content words and is classified as a JS shell; the crawler screenshot lacks streams, categories, and useful navigation content.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render core discovery content and real links, then hydrate interactive player and personalization features as enhancements.

findings.summary: Image delivery is not resolution- or format-efficient.
findings.evidence: Image evidence found 31 legacy PNG/JPEG images, no modern-format images, 13 oversized images, and 15 without responsive sources.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve appropriately sized AVIF/WebP where suitable, retain JPEG/PNG fallbacks where needed, and provide srcset/sizes.

findings.summary: Initial background and non-critical work is excessive.
findings.evidence: The page makes 252 requests and loads 148 scripts before a user chooses a stream; trace evidence shows 399.76ms blocking time.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load player variants, casting, experimentation, ads, and below-fold discovery code, and deprioritize background fetches.

findings.summary: The homepage media/script budget is heavy before explicit interaction.
findings.evidence: The initial route transfers 2.92MB and starts a featured live player while also loading ad, telemetry, casting, and extensive discovery code.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a poster-first player, defer autoplay/media and non-essential partners until intent or consent, and enforce route budgets.

findings.summary: Agent access relies on scraping a JavaScript-rendered shell.
findings.evidence: No structured agent capability was detected, and raw HTML exposes only 1% of rendered words despite public discovery and channel actions being useful to agents.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose stable machine-readable discovery/action affordances and, when mature, narrowly scoped WebMCP tools with confirmation for side effects.
